exam.disclaimer: **Important.** The format is compiled from public descriptions by university centres that run the state exam (UMCS, the University of Zielona Góra and others). The details — time, word limits, number of tasks, pass mark — differ between sources and change, so **always check the current samples at certyfikatpolski.pl** and the requirements of the centre where you'll sit the exam.
exam.levels.B1.parts.0.what: 4–5 tasks on understanding recordings. Each recording plays **twice**.
exam.levels.B1.parts.1.what: 4–5 tasks: notices, letters, articles. Multiple choice, matching, missing sentences.
exam.levels.B1.parts.2.what: 8–10 tasks: cases, verb forms, word choice, sentence transformations.
exam.levels.B1.parts.3.what: **Two texts**: a shorter one (≈ 25–50 words) and a longer one (≈ 150–175). Several task options to choose from.
exam.levels.B1.parts.4.what: Three tasks: **describing an illustration, a monologue, a situational conversation**. You get time for notes before answering.
exam.levels.B1.speaking.0.what: Describe what's in the picture: **place, people, actions, mood**. Explain what you think happened before and what will happen next.
exam.levels.B1.speaking.0.tip: Practise it in the «Speaking» section → Opis ilustracji.
exam.levels.B1.speaking.1.what: A statement on a topic following a plan: your experience, opinion, arguments. Aim for **1.5–2 minutes**.
exam.levels.B1.speaking.2.what: An everyday situation with the examiner (an agreement, a complaint, a request). Your ability to **react** to replies is assessed.
exam.levels.B1.speaking.2.tip: Answer the question, then add a detail of your own.
exam.levels.B1.writing.0.name: Krótki tekst (≈ 25–50 words)
exam.levels.B1.writing.0.what: SMS, message, invitation, short note. Cover every point of the task, politely and clearly.
exam.levels.B1.writing.1.name: Dłuższy tekst (≈ 150–175 words)
exam.levels.B1.writing.1.what: A letter (informal or formal), description, narrative. You need structure, connectors and the right register.
exam.levels.B2.parts.1.what: 4–5 tasks: articles, comments, official texts; you need to understand the author's position, not just the facts.
exam.levels.B2.parts.2.what: 8–10 tasks: complex sentences, the passive, participles, government, style.
exam.levels.B2.parts.3.what: Several tasks to choose from; **a shorter and a longer form**. Argumentation, formal and semi-formal texts. Word limits depend on the version (guide: up to ≈ 250).
exam.levels.B2.parts.4.what: Tasks based on illustrations and texts: **description, an argued statement, a situational conversation**. Check the number of tasks in a set in the samples.
exam.levels.B2.speaking.0.what: A description of the illustration + **interpretation**: why it is so, what it means, how you assess the situation.
exam.levels.B2.speaking.1.what: A claim or problem: **position, arguments, examples, counter-argument, conclusion**. Aim for 2–3 minutes.
exam.levels.B2.speaking.1.tip: Be sure to mention the other point of view and your response to it.
exam.levels.B2.speaking.2.what: A more complex situation: **negotiations, a complaint, persuasion**. React to objections, offer a compromise.
exam.levels.B2.writing.0.what: A business message, e-mail, notice, short reply — clear, in the right register.
exam.levels.B2.writing.0.tip: No more than 1 sentence per point + polite formulas.
exam.levels.B2.writing.1.what: An article, review, letter of complaint, **an argumentative text**: thesis, arguments «for» and «against», conclusion.
exam.levels.B2.writing.1.tip: A variety of connectors and structures — half of the «zakres środków» criterion.
exam.criteria.speaking.0.ua: whether the task is done: all points, topic, length
exam.criteria.speaking.1.ua: fluency, no long pauses, logical flow
exam.criteria.speaking.2.ua: range of vocabulary and grammatical structures
exam.criteria.writing.0.ua: all points of the task, length, form and register
strategies.0.title: The formula «thesis — reason — example»
strategies.0.body: When you don't know what to say, any question can be broken into three steps. It saves you from silence and gives a **natural structure** that the examiner assesses.
strategies.1.title: Forgot a word? Don't stop
strategies.1.body: In the exam **silence costs more than a mistake**. Replace the word with a description — that's valued as a communication strategy.
strategies.1.steps.0: «To jest taka rzecz, która służy do…» (it's a thing that is used for…)
strategies.1.steps.3: Don't apologise for every word — keep talking.
strategies.2.title: Preparation time isn't for writing
strategies.2.body: Notes are **5–6 keywords and the order of ideas**, not a text. Whoever writes full sentences then reads from the paper and loses fluency.
strategies.2.steps.0: Underline the task points — they are your plan.
strategies.2.steps.1: Next to each — 1–2 words and one example.
strategies.2.steps.2: Formulate the first two sentences fully in your head: a good start removes stress.
strategies.3.title: Task points = a checklist
strategies.3.body: The task lists what to cover. The examiner ticks boxes: **a missing point costs marks, even if the text is perfect**.
strategies.3.steps.0: Highlight all the points (usually 3–5) and number them.
strategies.3.steps.1: A separate sentence or paragraph for each.
strategies.3.steps.2: At the end go through the list: is each one covered?
strategies.3.steps.3: In our editor the points on the left tick themselves.
strategies.4.title: 75 minutes: how to split the time (B1)
strategies.4.body: The most common mistake — people write for a long time without checking. A split that works:
strategies.4.steps.0: **5 min** — read the task, choose an option, make a plan.
strategies.4.steps.2: **40 min** — the long text (a draft straight into the final version).
strategies.4.steps.3: **10 min** — proofread: commas, endings, diacritics, word limit.
strategies.5.title: A 3-minute check
strategies.5.body: Before handing in, go through the text **four times** — each time looking for just one thing:
strategies.5.steps.0: **Diacritics:** ą ę ć ł ń ó ś ź ż — are they all in place.
strategies.5.steps.1: **Commas:** before że, żeby, który, ponieważ, ale.
strategies.5.steps.2: **Endings:** cases after prepositions, gender of verbs in the past tense.
strategies.6.title: Practise aloud what you prepare in writing
strategies.6.body: The connectors and phrases you just used in a letter — **repeat them aloud**: that's how they move into your active vocabulary. Model answers on the site can be listened to and repeated sentence by sentence (shadowing).
strategies.7.title: Study rhythm: 30 minutes a day
strategies.7.body: Regularity matters more than long sessions. A working weekly scheme:
strategies.7.steps.0: **Mon:** new week — speaking (describing an illustration) + words.

friends.0.trap: The Ukrainian «склеп» is an underground vault, a crypt. You go **do sklepu** — to the shop.
friends.1.trap: «Poważna choroba» — a serious illness. The Ukrainian «поважний» means respected, not serious.
friends.2.trap: **Wyraz** is a word. «Вираз» (a phrase) in Polish is **wyrażenie**.
friends.3.trap: **Owoce** — fruit, while vegetables are **warzywa**. The Ukrainian «овочі» means **warzywa**!
friends.4.trap: **Urząd** is an office/authority (urząd miasta, urząd skarbowy). «Government» in Polish is **rząd**.
friends.5.trap: **Rząd** — both a government and a row (rząd krzeseł). Don't confuse it with **urząd**.
friends.6.trap: «Pilna sprawa» — an urgent matter; «pilny uczeń» — a diligent pupil. The Ukrainian «пильний» means attentive, watchful.
friends.7.trap: **Mów wolno** — speak slowly; **wolno tu palić?** — is smoking allowed here? Not just «free».
friends.8.trap: **Wynajmuję mieszkanie** — I rent a flat. The Ukrainian «мешкання» means a dwelling in general.
friends.9.trap: **Pokój** — a room (pokój gościnny) and peace. The Ukrainian «покій» is rarely used for «room».
errors.0.why: After **jako** — nominative. In Ukrainian «працюю лікарем» (instrumental) — Polish doesn't say that.
errors.2.why: **Podoba mi się** — «mi» (dative) goes before «się». «Mnie» doesn't occur here.
errors.3.why: **Czekać na** + accusative. In Ukrainian «чекаю тебе» — without a preposition.
errors.4.why: Before «w» + «wt-» you need **we** — it's easier to pronounce.
errors.5.why: **od** + genitive plural: od dwóch lat, od pięciu lat.
errors.8.why: Languages: **po polsku**, po ukraińsku, po angielsku.
errors.10.why: In greetings the Polish word order is different.
errors.11.why: In writing prefer **ponieważ / dlatego że**, not «dlatego bo».
